why:
The Vienna is your second White repertoire, alongside the London. Start with the king pawn and develop the queen-side knight. Against the two knight defences this repertoire offers the f-pawn; against the bishop defence it starts with bishop development.

The gambit is a trade-off, not a forced win: your central play comes with weaker diagonals around your king. Develop promptly, answer checks and central counterstrikes, and do not assume that every pawn sacrifice gives an attack.

This part covers Black's king-pawn reply only. Other first replies belong to later parts of the 1.e4 repertoire. The deeper branches are level-gated; start with the basic route and return for the alternatives.
